{{nihongo|'''Arei Shrine'''|阿禮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines the following three deities:
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}
* Emperor Hondawake (Hondawake no Sumeramikoto: the 15th {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}})

=== Overview ===
The Mae-gu (Front Shrine) is located in Shiojiri Town, Shiojiri City, while the Okusha (Inner Shrine) is located at Myōjindaira in Kakizawa, in the same city. The honden of the Mae-gu is built in the nagare-zukuri style with three bays and a copper roof. Between two one-bay nagare-zukuri shrine buildings, a doorway has been installed for the purpose of distant worship of the Okusha at Myōjindaira, giving the structure a distinctive design. The three shrines are known as Ōmiya Hachimangū, Arei Daimyōjin, and Shiojiri Daimyōjin, and are richly decorated with carvings from the mid-Edo period.

During the Sengoku period, the shrine received the patronage of the {{ill|Takeda clan|ar|عشيرة تاكيدا|ca|Clan Takeda|cs|Klan Takeda|de|Takeda (Klan)|eo|Takeda (klano)|es|Clan Takeda|eu|Takeda klana|fa|خاندان تاکدا|fr|Clan Takeda|glk|تاكدا كوگا|hu|Takeda-ház|id|Klan Takeda|it|Clan Takeda|ja|武田氏|ko|다케다씨|mk|Такеда (клан)|nl|Takeda (familie)|no|Takeda-klanen|pl|Takeda (ród)|pt|Clã Takeda|ru|Такэда|sr|Клан Такеда|th|ตระกูลทาเกดะ|tr|Takeda boyu|uk|Рід Такеда|zh|武田氏|qid=Q1210114}}, including donations of shrine lands.

According to shrine tradition, the shrine was originally located near the Iohata Rock on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Shiojiri Pass|ja|塩尻峠|zh|盐尻峠|qid=Q10434172}}, and was relocated to Myōjindaira in Kakizawa during the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}. With the establishment of {{ill|Shiojiri-shuku|Q3482312|qid=Q3482312}} on the {{ill|Nakasendō|ca|Nakasendō|de|Nakasendō|es|Nakasendō|fa|ناکاسندو|fr|Nakasendō|it|Nakasendō|ja|中山道|ko|나카센도|ms|Nakasendō|nl|Nakasendo|pl|Nakasendō|pt|Nakasendō|ru|Накасэндо|su|Nakasendō|sv|Nakasendō|th|นากาเซ็นโด|tr|Nakasendō|uk|Середгірський шлях|zh|中山道|qid=Q1154479}} in the early {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, only the Mae-gu was relocated to the western edge of the post town. The current parishioners consist of seven neighborhoods in the eastern district of Shiojiri: Kamimachi, Muromachi, Nakamachi, Miyamoto-machi, Horinouchi, Nagaune, and Sajiki. It is said that the ancient {{ill|Tōsandō|be|Тасанда|de|Tōsandō|es|Tōsandō|fa|توساندو|fr|Tōsandō|it|Tōsandō|ja|東山道|ko|도산도|lt|Tosando|pl|Tōsandō|pt|Tōsandō|ru|Тосандо|simple|Tōsandō|sr|Тосандо|tr|Tōsandō|uk|Східногірський край|zh|東山道|zh_min_nan|Tôsandô|zh_yue|東山道|qid=Q1334011}} post station “Kakushi Station” was located near this shrine.<ref>{{ill|Kadokawa Nihon Chimei Daijiten|ja|角川日本地名大辞典|ko|가도카와 일본 지명 대사전|ru|Большой словарь японских топонимов Кадокава|uk|Великий словник японських топонімів Кадокава|zh|角川日本地名大辭典|qid=Q4093011}} 20 Nagano Prefecture, p.306</ref>
